subject: NovusAI migration runway — Rightsize runway, bridge plan, and fallback matrix
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta@novusai.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: NovusAI Procurement <procurement@novusai.com>, Diego Alvarez <diego.alvarez@novusai.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NovusAI migration runway — Rightsize runway, bridge plan, and fallback matrix

Thanks again for the run-through this morning. A couple of follow-ups from our infra team:

- We currently see a 75th/95th token-length profile skewed toward shorter chats but with a small subset of long context requests (~3% > 4k tokens).
- Peak qps during our test window was ~1,200 requests/minute.

Can you confirm what buffer you recommend for the Dedicated commit and what the fallback looks like if we exceed committed throughput during the first 30 days? Also, please attach the latest sizing workbook — Diego will use it for procurement.

Appreciate it,
Marta

--
Marta Ruiz
Ops Lead, NovusAI
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@novusai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, NovusAI Procurement <procurement@novusai.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: NovusAI migration runway — Rightsize runway, bridge plan, and fallback matrix

Marta — thanks. Attaching the sizing workbook and a short runbook snapshot. Key notes up front:

- Baseline commit recommendation: 64 vGPU-equivalent slots (NVIDIA A100-equivalent logic) to cover the 95th percentile with a 15% buffer for autoscaling smoothing.
- Bridge capacity (first 30 days): keep an additional 16-slot warm pool to cover traffic bursts; warm pool billing on a reduced rate and automatically drained after day 30 unless opt-in.
- Fallback: automatic routing to smaller, latency-optimized hosted variants (same model family, 3-bit quant) when sustained over-commit detected for >10 minutes; fallback preserves 95% of QPS but increases 95th latency by ~60-120ms in our benchmarks.

Attachments: 20280316-sizing_matrix_v3.xlsx (xlsx), novus-migration-ma-plan-2028-03-16.pdf (pdf)

Action items: Diego to confirm the 30-day warm-pool acceptance; Novus procurement to review pricing addendum for warm pool.

Thanks,
Irene

--
Irene Choi
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Diego Alvarez <diego.alvarez@novusai.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_ichoi@redwood.ai>, Marta Ruiz <marta@novusai.com>
Cc: NovusAI Procurement <procurement@novusai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Mar 2028 08:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: NovusAI migration runway — Rightsize runway, bridge plan, and fallback matrix

Irene / team — quick confirmation: the sizing workbook assumes 8 concurrent tokens-per-request average for the short chats and scales for the 3% long requests. Can you add a sensitivity line for a scenario where long requests are 7% of traffic? Procurement needs the cost delta for that headroom.

Diego

--
Diego Alvarez
SRE Lead, NovusAI
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Alvarez <diego.alvarez@novusai.com>, Irene Choi <irene_ichoi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Mar 2028 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: NovusAI migration runway — Rightsize runway, bridge plan, and fallback matrix

Diego — good catch. I added two sensitivity rows to the workbook: 3% long-request baseline and a conservative 7% long-request case. TL;DR: going from 3% to 7% increases baseline slot need from 64 -> 78 (reserve + warm-pool unchanged). Cost delta for the committed tier (12-month) is ~+18% on committed GPU line items; warm-pool charges scale linearly with slot count.

Notes on mitigations:
- If Novus wants to lock in the lower 64-slot commit today, we recommend configuring a higher fallback threshold for the first two weeks (auto-scale trigger at 85% instead of 90%) and run daily traffic mirroring to catch acceptance regressions.
- Alternative: short term burst credits (one-off) to absorb unexpected surge while you validate model throttling.

Ben

--
Ben Carter
Principal Capacity Planner, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: NovusAI Procurement <procurement@novusai.com>, Diego Alvarez <diego.alvarez@novusai.com>, Irene Choi <irene_ichoi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: NovusAI migration runway — Rightsize runway, bridge plan, and fallback matrix

Diego / procurement team — following up with recommended commercial packaging:

1) Commit package A (conservative): 78-slot 12-month Reserved, includes automatic 24/7 warm pool at 20% capacity and 2000 mirroring minutes/month.
2) Commit package B (opportunistic): 64-slot 12-month Reserved + 16-slot 30-day warm pool (auto-opt-out), with optional one-time burst credits (100k token credits) priced separately.

Please review the attached pricing addendum (embedded in the HubSpot link). If you plan to pilot with option B, we can schedule a 48-hour smoke on the dedicated fleet next week and enable the traffic mirroring hooks.

Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: NovusAI migration runway — Rightsize runway, bridge plan, and fallback matrix

Thanks — NovusAI will take Commit package B to prioritize cost predictability while we validate the 30-day warm pool in staging. Procurement will sign the SOW today. Two requests before we flip:

- Can you confirm the exact SLA delta when the warm pool is active vs after day 30? We need the wording for the procurement addendum.
- Please confirm the orchestration play for a sustained 12-minute over-commit where fallback is triggered (we want the automatic steps and any manual approval gates documented).

If you can send the small addendum with the SLA bullets + the step-by-step orchestration play we can attach to the SOW.

Best,
Marta
